description: Register a new passkey, as an authenticator does for WebAuthn's navigator.credentials.create(): an ES256 (P-256) key pair is made here, the private key stored in the vault exactly as Bitwarden's own apps store a passkey (so they can sign with it too), and the answer is what a browser needs to finish the registration: the credential id, the attestation object (format none), the authenticator data and the public key (SPKI). The private key is never in the answer. It goes into the login item_id names, else into the one login already saved for this site with this username and no passkey, else into a new login named after the site (filed like create_login). Refused as excluded when the site's exclude list names a passkey the vault holds, and as unsupported when the site accepts no ES256 key. Use it for an agent's own identity; a person's own passkeys belong on their own devices.

algorithms.description: The COSE algorithm ids in the request's pubKeyCredParams, e.g. [-7, -257]. Empty means the default, which includes ES256 (-7).

client_data_hash.description: SHA-256 of the client data JSON for this request, base64url. An attestation of format none signs nothing, so it is only checked.

collection.description: For a new login: a collection name from health.

exclude_credentials.description: The request's excludeCredentials ids: passkeys the site already holds for this account.

items.description: A credential id, base64url as WebAuthn's JSON carries it.

item_id.description: The login to put it in: one without a passkey, or whose passkey is for the same account on this site (it is replaced).

resident_key.description: Whether the passkey is discoverable (a resident key), as the request's authenticatorSelection asks.

rp_id.description: The RP ID: the site's domain the passkey is bound to, e.g. example.com or login.example.com.

rp_name.description: The site's name as the request gives it (rp.name).

id.description: The site's id for the account (user.id), base64url, 1 to 64 bytes.

name.description: The account's name at the site (user.name), usually its email or username.

user_verified.description: Whether the user was verified for this request, which sets the UV flag. True only when the caller verified them: an agent signing in as its own identity, or a person who approved the request.

name: create_passkey
title: Create passkey
